title: Learning Brain Representation with Hierarchical Visual Embeddings
claim: A single shared brain-and-multi-encoder alignment backbone supports two tasks: retrieval in the fused space, or reconstruction by conditioning a frozen generator.
layout: 2 panels side by side, left-to-right flow, colored background regions group modules
description: Two side-by-side pipeline diagrams, (a) Brain-to-image retrieval and (b) Brain-to-image reconstruction. Each has a beige top band for brain encoding. A brain-signal and cupcake-image input goes through Wb, then an MLP with a residual connection, then LayerNorm, ending in a tan Brain Embedding bar. A pink lower band holds K parallel visual encoders f_v, each followed by a projection W_v. Their outputs are summed and passed through MLP and LN to give a tan Fusion Embedding bar. A dashed 'Contrastive Learning' box with a vertical double arrow links the two embeddings. In (a), a teal column on the right shows retrieved images, with the cupcake highlighted in red. In (b), the teal column holds an MLP, an IP-Adapter and a UNet (ε_θ), and ends in a generated dessert photo. Flame icons mark trainable modules and snowflake icons mark frozen ones. Muted blue and green blocks.
caption: Learning pipelines. Left: Retrieval objective that aligns the brain embedding $z_b$ with the fused visual embedding $z_f$ (HVF over $K$ pretrained encoders) using a symmetric InfoNCE; evaluation is nearest-neighbor retrieval in the fused space. Right: Reconstruction pipeline with a frozen, pretrained fusion prior—HVF plus a Conditioning Adapter (MLP projector + IP-Adapter with decoupled cross-attention). We contrastively align $z_b$ to the frozen $z_f$, project to $z_c$, and inject $z_c$ into a frozen SDXL UNet to synthesize the image. Visual encoders and the UNet are frozen; only the brain side is updated during alignment.
abstract: Decoding visual representations from brain signals has attracted significant attention in both neuroscience and artificial intelligence. However, the degree to which brain signals truly encode visual information remains unclear. Current visual decoding approaches explore various brain-image alignment strategies, yet most emphasize high-level semantic features while neglecting pixel-level details, thereby limiting our understanding of the human visual system. In this paper, we propose a brain-image alignment strategy that leverages multiple pre-trained visual encoders with distinct inductive biases to capture hierarchical and multi-scale visual representations, while employing a contrastive learning objective to achieve effective alignment between brain signals and visual embeddings. Furthermore, we introduce a Fusion Prior, which learns a stable mapping on large-scale visual data and subsequently matches brain features to this pre-trained prior, thereby enhancing distributional consistency across modalities. Extensive quantitative and qualitative experiments demonstrate that our method achieves a favorable balance between retrieval accuracy and reconstruction fidelity.
